title: Louis Armstrong arrives and the Roseland opening
summary: Henderson hires Armstrong from Chicago; Scott and Elmer Chambers look after him and he makes a sensation at Roseland.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, it got around, began getting around, Fletcher's name began to go up and everybody came to hear Fletcher, Fletcher, Fletcher, Fletcher. Then he wanted to expand his band. He wanted to get two more men. And he told us he was trying to get another trumpet player. That was Louis Armstrong, from -- he was out there in Chicago with Joe Oliver, the old man, Joe Oliver.

Well, we finally got Louis and he came to the band. He had high shoes on, button shoes. And a cardboard suitcase, and his stomach was way out like this. And they'd never been to New York before, and naturally, Broadway -- (unintelligible). But Alma and me, because we were the other trumpet players, we

took them in our hands, to ease his mind, and everything, and make him feel at home. Alma was a swell guy, too. He played trumpet, I played second and Louis was third, and took solos. See, I'd taken solos myself, but when Louis started to play -- whew, that was it.

Nothing like that had been heard before in New York, nothing like the way Louis played. He brought that New Orleans stuff here, and he played just a couple of nights there, and we left there. We had to open at Roseland. That's 51st Street and Broadway. That took up the whole block there. They had two bands there, one white and a big colored band.

Louis played that opening night at Roseland, and my goodness, people stopped dancing to come around and listen to him. He was scared at first. He said, how am I doing, Scottie? I said, listen, what I said, just close your eyes and play what you feel in your heart, in your body, in your mind. Just let it go, Louis, be yourself, that's all. Forget about the people. So he did. And they could hear him out in the street. And we were told that there were some people passing by that stopped, listening to him. He was so loud.

But he played. Well, that was the first night. The next night, you couldn't get in the place. Just that quick. It had gone all around about this new trumpet player at Roseland. Well, we had a great time there, we had a great time. We had a great time.
